bottleneck: CRISPR-Cas complexes bind and cut genomic sites beyond the intended target when mismatches or bulges in the guide RNA still permit binding. Off-target indels can cause frameshifts or disrupt gene regulation, and in the worst case hit tumor suppressors or proto-oncogenes, risking oncogenic transformation. Mismatch tolerance depends on sequence context, chromatin state, cell type, and dosage, making outcomes hard to predict computationally.
current_state: High-fidelity Cas variants and improved guide design reduce but do not eliminate off-target activity. The FDA's 2026 guidance now recommends NGS-based chromosomal integrity analysis for DSB-creating editors, reflecting that detection, not prevention, is the current frontier.

title: CRISPR off-target edits remain unpredictable
why_it_blocks: Unpredictable edits make regulators demand exhaustive safety data and keep germline and systemic in vivo editing near the ethical red line. Each unresolved off-target question slows clinical translation of otherwise curative edits.
